provenance: Original measurable objectives for the user-requested algorithms, architecture and communication enhancement; supplements rather than replaces the original specification.

domains.title: Algorithms from invariants through assembly to C abstractions

subtopics.title: Specifications, invariants and resource bounds

objectives.text: Derive an input/output relation, representation invariant and decreasing termination measure for an original bounded state trace.
Compute exact operation counts for contrasting input families and distinguish worst-case, expected and amortized claims with their assumptions.
Find a counterexample to an intentionally weakened invariant and identify the first transition that invalidates it.

subtopics.title: Arrays, links and frontier representations

objectives.text: Derive byte offsets, valid index ranges and ownership links for reused array/list/stack/queue representations without rebuilding their complete implementations.
Trace the same bounded operation sequence in contiguous and linked representations and account for live storage, traversal work and failed operations.
Explain which representation invariant survives a storage-policy change and verify that no stale reference escapes the selected policy.

subtopics.title: Callable hand-written x86-64 and Thumb kernels

objectives.text: Write original scalar search kernels in separate x86-64 SysV and Cortex-M4 Thumb assembly files and expose checked C declarations.
Derive register liveness, signed/unsigned flag predicates, preserved-register obligations and stack alignment for each kernel and a nested-call probe.
Demonstrate ABI preservation and bounded memory access using adversarial inputs, poisoned scratch registers, sentinels and captured disassembly.

subtopics.title: Ordering, searching and partition boundaries

objectives.text: Derive a half-open lower-bound search invariant and progress argument for duplicate, absent and boundary keys.
Translate that invariant into a hand-written assembly kernel with an explicit element width and overflow-safe address calculation.
Compare operation counts with the reused C implementation and reject an off-by-one or signedness mutation with a concrete smallest counterexample.

subtopics.title: Sorting, permutation and stability

objectives.text: Derive preservation of the sorted prefix, multiset and tagged equal-key order during bounded insertion and merge transitions.
Write a small original assembly insertion kernel while reusing the prior full merge/heap sort implementations for differential evidence.
Measure comparisons and moves on sorted, reverse and duplicate-rich inputs and separate asymptotic evidence from machine timing.

subtopics.title: Heap invariants and priority policies

objectives.text: Derive the local precondition and moving violation for sift-down in the reused zero-origin heap representation.
Replace only the bounded sift-down kernel with original assembly and preserve the prior heap API and duplicate policy.
Recompute heap order and key multiplicity independently after each transition and account for height-bounded work without claiming the whole heap was rebuilt.

subtopics.title: Trees, rotations and representation-preserving change

objectives.text: Derive inorder, height and balance effects of single and double rotations and of a deletion rebalance path in the prior AVL implementation.
Instrument the reused tree to emit state certificates and verify parent/child reachability, duplicate policy and cached metadata after each mutation.
Compare balanced and degenerate search paths on the same keys and explain the difference between functional equivalence and resource bounds.

subtopics.title: Hash probes and bounded string matching

objectives.text: Derive probe reachability through empty, occupied and deleted slots and identify the assumptions behind expected lookup bounds.
Write a bounded assembly probe/search kernel over the prior hash representation and a small original C byte-span matcher with an explicit empty-pattern policy.
Verify collision, wraparound, full-table, tombstone and embedded-zero cases while counting probes or byte comparisons independently.

subtopics.title: Graph frontiers, shortest paths and historical refinement

objectives.text: Derive the distinction between BFS layers, tentative weighted distances and settled vertices from a small original graph trace.
Reuse the earlier queue and priority heap to implement a bounded graph adapter with nonnegative weights, checked distance addition and disconnected results.
Validate distances and predecessor paths against independent tiny-graph enumeration and explain why a negative edge or an invalid settle rule breaks the chosen argument.

subtopics.title: Higher C abstractions over invariant-preserving kernels

objectives.text: Design a typed wrapper and an explicit context/callback interface over a reused container or new assembly kernel without delegating the educational algorithm to libc.
State ownership, comparator consistency, failure atomicity and iterator invalidation contracts and distinguish pointer collections from byte-copy value storage.
Show identical observable results across the chosen typed and generic adapters, with independently checked lifetime, error and representation evidence.

domains.title: Computer and microcontroller architecture from state to evidence

subtopics.title: Architectural state and implementation models

objectives.text: Define registers, memory, instruction state and external inputs for a small abstract machine and trace its state transitions.
Separate ISA-visible behavior from datapath, pipeline, cache and board integration choices using a paired x86-64/Cortex-M4 comparison.
Classify each claimed observation as a model result, executable ISA result or physical device measurement and record its unresolved assumptions.

subtopics.title: Boolean logic, ALU slices and finite arithmetic

objectives.text: Derive full-adder and subtraction truth tables from Boolean equations and compose a four-bit ripple-carry model.
Compute result, zero, sign, carry and overflow flags for every four-bit input pair and distinguish carry from signed overflow.
Relate the model to inspected x86 and Arm condition flags while explaining why machine wraparound does not establish defined C signed overflow.

subtopics.title: Registers, addresses and representation boundaries

objectives.text: Derive effects of byte, word and doubleword operations on complete x86-64 register state and contrast the selected Thumb widths.
Reconstruct values from an explicit little-endian byte sequence and calculate base/index/scale/displacement addresses with bounds.
Demonstrate that aligned addresses, hardware accessibility and C object/effective-type permission are separate obligations in a reused typed or byte-storage example.

subtopics.title: Instruction formats, decoding and branch targets

objectives.text: Decode a bounded selected x86 instruction’s prefix/opcode/operand fields and a selected Thumb instruction’s halfwords from their actual bytes.
Compute relative branch targets and explain the distinction between instruction width, architectural PC behavior and assembler syntax.
Cross-check hand decoding with vendor definitions and disassembly while rejecting a deliberately wrong displacement or width assumption.

subtopics.title: Datapath, clocked state and control

objectives.text: Build a small original register/ALU/load/store datapath state model with explicit next-state and commit rules.
Trace fetch, decode, operand selection, execution and update for a declared toy instruction sequence and identify the control signals required.
Explain why the toy model is not a faithful Cortex-M4 or x86 microarchitecture and distinguish combinational output from clocked stored state.

subtopics.title: Pipeline hazards, forwarding and control changes

objectives.text: Produce a stage-by-cycle schedule for a declared five-stage in-order model including a RAW dependency and load-use delay.
Derive the effect of forwarding, a stall and a taken-branch flush on the same instruction stream and count retired instructions and cycles.
Explain why RAW dependence, pipeline hazard and data race are distinct and limit any extrapolation to a physical CPU.

subtopics.title: Memory hierarchy, locality and cache costs

objectives.text: Derive cache index/tag/offset and hit/miss outcomes for a small specified cache and original address trace.
Compute AMAT and a declared in-order stall estimate with consistent units, then compare two layouts without equating misses with execution time.
Identify compulsory, capacity or conflict mechanisms within the stated model and separate model results from measured cache behavior.

subtopics.title: Microcontroller memory, buses and DMA reachability

objectives.text: Map CPU and DMA masters to documented STM32F4 memory targets and explain the CCM versus ordinary SRAM reachability boundary.
Derive a linker-placement and DMA-buffer decision from exact part/revision evidence and document ownership and completion ordering separately.
Trace arbitration and peripheral-bridge constraints in a static model and record which throughput or electrical claims require real device measurements.

subtopics.title: Reset, exceptions and architectural boundaries

objectives.text: Trace reset vector selection and a basic Cortex-M4 exception entry/return state using previously inspected startup and core passages.
Compare a subroutine call’s ABI preservation with exception stacking and priority behavior without treating them as interchangeable.
Verify a saved original frame/return trace and state the limits of emulator observations, optional FP state and device-specific boot configuration.

subtopics.title: Performance equations and credible experiments

objectives.text: Compute CPU time and whole-task speedup from original instruction/CPI/frequency and Amdahl inputs with dimensionally checked arithmetic.
Design a bounded experiment comparing reused C and hand-written kernels with identical results, captured toolchain/CPU settings and repeated measurements.
Report the measurement distribution and confounders, distinguish algorithmic work from elapsed time, and avoid emulator-based WCET or energy conclusions.

domains.title: Serial, differential and CAN communication interfaces

subtopics.title: MCU architecture and the peripheral/transceiver boundary

objectives.text: Draw a selected F439 communication path from C buffer through CPU/bus/MMIO, peripheral and transceiver to wire, and assign framing, arbitration and electrical responsibilities to the correct component.
Derive clock, pin alternate-function, voltage-domain and DMA-memory prerequisites for a selected peripheral without treating generic Cortex-M features as SoC guarantees.
Create separate host-fixture, target-register and physical-measurement evidence gates and state precisely which electrical claims an emulator cannot establish.

subtopics.title: UART asynchronous framing, baud and completion

objectives.text: Encode and decode bounded 8N1 and parity-enabled UART traces with LSB-first data, start/stop boundaries and deliberate framing/parity failures.
Compute F439 BRR encodings and realized baud error from the selected peripheral clock and oversampling mode, then compare the result with a measured bit period.
Implement bounded transmit/receive status handling that distinguishes TXE from final TC and records overrun/framing failures without an unbounded wait.

subtopics.title: USART synchronous mode and clocked sampling

objectives.text: Configure a bounded F439 USART synchronous-master transfer with declared CPOL, CPHA and last-clock-pulse policy, and predict CK/TX/RX traces.
Explain and demonstrate why synchronous USART reception needs transmitted clock-generating data and why start/stop handling differs from a generic SPI transaction.
Verify configuration changes occur with transmitter/receiver disabled and compare the captured synchronous trace with the asynchronous UART trace.

subtopics.title: I2C electrical signaling, pull-ups and arbitration

objectives.text: Compute a feasible pull-up interval from selected supply, sink-current limit, rise-time target and bounded bus capacitance, and reject an empty interval.
Trace wired-AND SDA/SCL behavior, START/STOP/repeated START, clock stretching and two-controller arbitration including identical-prefix cases.
Measure rise time and low levels on a declared Standard/Fast-mode setup and explain why logic-analyzer decoding alone cannot establish electrical compliance.

subtopics.title: I2C transaction state, ACK/NACK and recovery

objectives.text: Implement a bounded 7-bit write/read transaction model with explicit address direction, repeated START, per-byte ACK and terminal-read NACK.
Separate address/data NACK, lost arbitration, stretched-clock timeout and stuck SDA/SCL into distinct results while preserving ownership and bounded retry policy.
Exercise conditional nine-clock bus clear only for SDA-low/SCL-releasable cases and verify success/failure/post-reset states without inferring target register semantics from the bus specification.

subtopics.title: SPI sampling, chip-select framing and driver ownership

objectives.text: Implement a checked bounded full-duplex SPI transaction that derives target width/clock/select timing, models all four CPOL/CPHA sampling modes and preserves MOSI/MISO direction.
Trace F439 polling/interrupt/DMA buffer ownership, drain receive data and wait for final completion before chip-select release, rejecting overrun, stale reuse and cancelled in-flight transfers.
Verify an original transaction scheduler with explicit lengths, dummy bytes, lifetimes and timeout/error results against four-mode, failed and cancelled traces plus a bounded physical capture.

subtopics.title: RS-232 voltage conversion, polarity and DTE/DCE

objectives.text: Map logic-side UART idle/data through a selected MAX3232 driver/receiver and predict the inverted positive/negative RS-232 line voltage.
Produce an exact DTE/DCE signal-direction and connector-pin table for a selected point-to-point link, including reference ground and optional handshake exclusions.
Measure a bounded 3.3-V-logic RS-232 loopback at a declared safe rate/load and correlate logic/wire captures without connecting RS-232 voltage directly to MCU pins.

subtopics.title: RS-422 one-driver differential multidrop

objectives.text: Design a one-driver, two-receiver RS-422 topology with declared differential polarity, end termination, reference path and device input limits.
Distinguish RS-422 one-driver multidrop from RS-485 multipoint and from full-duplex UART framing or application addressing.
Compare two receiver observations of the same transmitted pattern and diagnose swapped pair, absent termination and disconnected receiver cases with bounded electrical evidence.

subtopics.title: RS-485 multipoint direction, loading and byte-channel contract

objectives.text: Design a short two-node half-duplex bus with explicit termination, bias/failsafe policy, unit-load budget, reference path and one-transmitter-at-a-time rule.
Implement an RS-485 byte-channel state machine that accounts for driver enable, conditional wake/enable delay, UART TC, disable delay and receiver turnaround.
Capture DE, logic TX and differential bus timing, prove no premature last-stop-bit truncation or overlapping drivers, and expose reusable bounded byte/error events for T40.

subtopics.title: Classic CAN framing, arbitration and error confinement

objectives.text: Trace dominant0/recessive1 bitwise arbitration across bounded 11-bit and 29-bit classic frame examples, including data/remote and standard/extended comparisons.
Parse a declared classic CAN data-frame subset with DLC, payload, stuffing and CRC/ACK/EOF boundaries while separating link ACK from application delivery.
Classify bounded arbitration, retry, error-active/passive and bus-off traces using the inspected source scope and reject claims of complete fault-confinement conformance.

subtopics.title: F439 bxCAN timing, filters, mailboxes and receive ownership

objectives.text: Derive legal BRP/BS1/BS2/SJW register encodings, realized bitrate and sample point from a selected APB clock and distinguish timing derivation from measured transceiver propagation.
Implement a bounded mailbox/filter/FIFO model that separates identifier-based content filtering from destination addresses and releases received entries exactly once.
Verify mailbox success/arbitration-loss/transmit-error and both FIFO-overrun policies, then document classic-only capability and bounded bus-off recovery assumptions.

subtopics.title: CAN FD ISO format, dual bitrate and external-controller boundary

objectives.text: Encode and validate the ISO CAN FD DLC mapping, FDF/BRS/ESI metadata and 0–64-byte data-only subset, and distinguish FD from pre-ISO framing and classic remote frames.
Explain selected 17/21-bit CRC, protected stuff count, fixed stuffing and transmitter-delay-compensation responsibilities without claiming a complete conformant FD encoder.

Design an F439-to-external-FD-controller transaction/power boundary with checked SPI word framing and capability evidence; distinguish core software verification from optional measured physical FD closure.

domains.title: Ethernet, OSI and MCU frame-channel foundations

subtopics.title: OSI services, peer protocols and Internet layer mapping

objectives.text: Classify an original endpoint trace into service interface, peer protocol, SDU and PDU roles and identify where encapsulation/demultiplexing changes representation.
Map seven OSI layer purposes onto a finite Internet endpoint without inventing one protocol/library per layer or equating sockets with the whole stack.
Produce a layer responsibility table that distinguishes physical faults, link errors, network forwarding, transport reliability and application semantics, including L2 bridging.

subtopics.title: Ethernet physical media and PHY responsibilities

objectives.text: Describe a selected 100BASE-TX copper path from MAC through RMII, PHY and magnetics to cable while locating signaling/coding/link negotiation outside the F439 MAC.
Distinguish line rate from application throughput and shared half-duplex collision behavior from switched full-duplex operation for the declared lab topology.
Record exact board/PHY/media/clock identities and measure link establishment or loss without treating a synthetic frame trace or QEMU run as physical evidence.

subtopics.title: Ethernet frame, padding, FCS and buffer boundaries

objectives.text: Build and parse bounded untagged Ethernet frames with exact destination/source/type-or-length fields, declared 46–1500-byte payload/pad rules and malformed-length rejection.
Distinguish seven-byte preamble, SFD, frame bytes, minimum frame, FCS and interpacket timing from the byte buffer exposed by a selected MAC/driver API.
Verify FCS coverage and MAC padding/CRC configuration against an independent bounded oracle and record when received length includes FCS or hardware stripping changes the buffer contract.

subtopics.title: MAC addressing, filtering and switching boundaries

objectives.text: Decode I/G and U/L address bits, broadcast and selected multicast/local-unicast addresses without confusing Ethernet MAC addresses with IPv4 addresses or CAN identifiers.
Trace a bounded learning-bridge table through learning, known-unicast forwarding, unknown-unicast flooding and expiry, distinguishing each from IP routing.
Configure or model selected endpoint receive filters and explain why a switched port or promiscuous receiver does not automatically observe every network frame.

subtopics.title: MII/RMII, MDIO and PHY link negotiation

objectives.text: Derive the selected RMII two-bit data and shared 50-MHz reference-clock contract and distinguish it from MII and the MDIO/MDC management interface.
Perform bounded PHY identity/status/negotiation queries using the exact inspected LAN8742A register scope and handle link-down or incomplete negotiation as explicit results.
Translate the actual negotiated speed/duplex into MAC configuration and compare register/capture evidence while preserving exact board revision, pin and solder-bridge assumptions.

subtopics.title: F439 MAC/DMA initialization and reachable memory

objectives.text: Draw the MAC, FIFO, DMA, descriptor and buffer path and prove selected storage is reachable by Ethernet DMA rather than placed in CPU-only CCM.
Construct a bounded initialization dependency order for clocks, reset, RMII selection, PHY result, MAC filtering, descriptor bases and independent MAC/DMA start controls.
State compiler/hardware ordering and ownership publication conditions and verify failure returns for missing clock, invalid memory region or absent physical link without importing an M7 cache recipe.

subtopics.title: Ethernet receive descriptors, validation and recycling

objectives.text: Implement a bounded normal-descriptor receive model that separates DMA OWN, FS/LS, FL-including-CRC and ES/DE error status before exposing frame bytes.
Reject partial, truncated, over-capacity and error-marked receive chains while preserving consumer buffer lifetime and exactly-once recycling.
Exercise receive-buffer-unavailable and consumer-backpressure traces, then expose a checked frame-channel interface for T41 with explicit FCS and length policy.

subtopics.title: Ethernet transmit descriptors, completion and recovery

objectives.text: Implement bounded normal-descriptor transmit publication with complete frame/FS/LS metadata established before the first ownership handoff.
Separate queued, DMA-owned, completed and failed states; apply declared CRC/padding policy and reject premature buffer reuse or unbounded retry.
Verify ring-full, partial-publication, failed completion and reset-drain traces with bounded counters/timeouts and report what MAC/DMA tests do not prove about the wire.

subtopics.title: From Ethernet to IPv4, TCP and HTTP responsibility contracts

objectives.text: Trace one bounded HTTP exchange through Ethernet, ARP/IPv4, TCP and HTTP responsibilities and identify each header, checksum, endpoint namespace and validation owner.
Specify reusable frame-channel handoff, time/event service and bounded buffer ownership for T41 without delegating L2–L4 to an operating-system socket.
Declare the finite educational endpoint exclusions and distinguish Ethernet, IPv4, TCP and HTTP subset evidence from claims of complete standard or Internet-host conformance.

subtopics.title: Cross-layer timing, fault localization and evidence

objectives.text: Correlate a deterministic host frame trace, target descriptor events, PHY status and external packet capture using explicit clocks and capture points.
Localize bounded failures such as cable loss, receive CRC error, full descriptor ring, unreachable next hop, transport timeout and malformed HTTP to the first failed contract.
Compute layered payload/overhead and latency budgets for the declared exchange and maintain separate software, board and physical acceptance receipts.

subtopics.title: Model, service boundaries and ownership

objectives.text: Distinguish OSI reference-model responsibilities from a particular protocol suite and Internet architecture.
Trace an application record through all seven original layer PDUs and both physical segments.
Specify ownership, capacities, addressing scope and error publication at every service boundary.

subtopics.title: RS-485 physical adapter and medium access

objectives.text: Wire and measure the declared 3.3-V transceiver, terminations and two independent half-duplex segments.
Implement UART transmit-complete, driver-enable guards and master-granted turns without overlapping drivers.
Separate real physical timing/disconnect evidence from deterministic host octet traces.

subtopics.title: Link framing and error detection

objectives.text: Encode and incrementally validate the exact bounded delimiter/escape/header/CRC frame contract.
Recover framing after truncation, noise, bad escaping, foreign addresses and overlong input.
Demonstrate local-link delivery and drop counters without attributing end-to-end reliability to CRC.

subtopics.title: Network addressing, routing and hop limits

objectives.text: Keep link next-hop addresses distinct from end-to-end node addresses and service ports.
Forward between the two segments by the exact static route table while preserving end-to-end fields.
Predict and verify unknown-route, hop-limit and ownership failures at the intermediate router.

subtopics.title: Reliable bounded transport and flow state

objectives.text: Segment and atomically reassemble bounded messages using the exact transfer/fragment contract.
Trace matching acknowledgments, retransmission, duplicates and credit probes with an injected clock.
Prove that failed or blocked transfers publish no partial message and free their bounded state.

subtopics.title: Session dialogue and resynchronization

objectives.text: Negotiate schema/units and enforce explicit dialogue-token ownership independently of transport state.
Use per-direction checkpoints to suppress repeated application effects after a retained-state resume.
Distinguish successful RAM-state resume from stale epoch, incompatible negotiation and reboot refusal.

subtopics.title: Presentation syntax and typed representation

objectives.text: Convert between local typed values and canonical bounded TLVs without copying native struct layout.
Validate ordering, uniqueness, signed range, units and UTF-8 before publishing a decoded record.
Show that presentation encoding changes no routing, transport or application semantic authority.

subtopics.title: Application exchange and seven-layer acceptance

objectives.text: Implement the exact GET/SET/REPLY semantics and unchanged-state error contract.
Correlate request IDs, checkpoints, ports, node addresses and link frames in one routed worked trace.
Collect independent fault oracles and actual physical captures to close the whole educational stack.

subtopics.title: Protocol subset, interfaces and bounded resources

objectives.text: Declare the controlled same-link interoperability profile and excluded full-host requirements.
Trace nested Ethernet/ARP or Ethernet/IPv4/TCP/HTTP lengths and buffer ownership.
Define byte-span APIs that preserve packet boundaries below TCP and byte-stream continuity above it.

subtopics.title: Ethernet PHY, RMII and physical readiness

objectives.text: Locate the F439 MAC, external LAN8742A PHY, RMII clock, magnetics and cable boundaries.
Read PHY identity, reset/link/negotiation status with exact latch and timeout semantics before marking readiness.
Measure actual board/link operation and distinguish it from loopback, TAP or mocked-register evidence.

subtopics.title: MAC and Ethernet DMA descriptor lifecycle

objectives.text: Initialize bounded RX/TX rings in DMA-accessible memory using the selected actual controller contract.
Publish/reclaim descriptor and frame ownership with ordering, first/last and error checks.
Calculate the exposed frame length with padding and CRC handled exactly once and recover from unavailable buffers.

subtopics.title: Ethernet demultiplexing and ARP neighbor state

objectives.text: Validate the exact untagged Ethernet II and Ethernet/IPv4 ARP fields before dispatch or cache updates.
Resolve only the declared peer with bounded cache, queued datagram, retry and expiry state.
Explain and verify foreign-destination, spoofed-field, VLAN, stale-cache and unresolved-peer outcomes.

subtopics.title: IPv4, ICMP echo and Internet checksum

objectives.text: Parse bounded fixed IPv4 headers and verify total length, flags, destination and header checksum.
Compute one’s-complement checksums across odd spans and the TCP pseudo-header without undefined arithmetic.
Reply to the exact ICMP echo subset and expose fragment/option omissions as restricted-profile limitations.

subtopics.title: TCP handshake, sequence and close state

objectives.text: Implement passive handshake, MSS parsing and modular sequence/ACK validation for the declared one-connection profile.
Preserve exactly the accepted in-order byte stream under duplicates, prefix overlap and packet segmentation.
Trace FIN, peer half-close, simultaneous close, reset and TIME-WAIT without treating them as HTTP framing.

subtopics.title: TCP timers, flow pressure and conservative sending

objectives.text: Update retransmission estimates and backoff using only admissible RTT samples and an injected monotonic clock.
Enforce peer usable window, local capacity, zero-window probes and one outstanding segment without byte loss.
Compare conservative lab behavior with unimplemented general-host congestion/event requirements and record its limits.

subtopics.title: HTTP reuse, independent interoperability and physical closure

objectives.text: Attach the previously verified T42 HTTP core through an adapter that preserves stream bytes and bounded ownership.
Verify ARP, echo, handshake, HTTP response, loss, zero-window and close traces with an independent peer.
Close actual cable-loss/recovery and board reset-incarnation evidence without counting simulated packets as L1 success.

domains.title: From-scratch HTTP server over OS sockets

subtopics.title: Socket lifecycle and layer ownership

objectives.text: Create a loopback listener and bounded accepted-connection table with explicit descriptor flags and cleanup.
Separate application/parser ownership from OS TCP/IP and physical responsibilities.
Handle accept/readiness races and descriptor-limit failures without blocking the event loop or leaking state.

subtopics.title: Incremental request grammar and target authority

objectives.text: Parse request lines and headers incrementally as octets across every selected split and coalescing boundary.
Validate the declared origin-form and bounded absolute-form targets and the single HTTP1.1 Host contract.
Reject ambiguous whitespace, control bytes and obsolete folding before publishing a request.

subtopics.title: Header normalization and unambiguous message framing

objectives.text: Select exactly one NONE, Content-Length or final chunked body mode after bounded syntax validation.
Reject duplicate lengths, TE+CL, overflow and unsupported coding with the exact error/close policy.
Distinguish method semantics from body framing and preserve all unconsumed bytes for the next request.

subtopics.title: Chunked decoding, extensions and trailers

objectives.text: Decode chunk sizes, bounded extensions, data and terminal trailers incrementally without arithmetic overflow.
Keep trailer fields separate from original routing/framing headers and discard them under the declared policy.
Verify premature EOF and limit failures at every chunk state without publishing partial body data.

subtopics.title: HTTP semantics, routing and response serialization

objectives.text: Implement exact GET/HEAD /health and POST /echo contracts with matching status and bounded representations.
Serialize octet lengths, HEAD metadata, deterministic Date and allowed-method errors without header injection.
Respond immediately to admissible100-continue or header-determined final errors without waiting for the body.

subtopics.title: Partial output, persistence and pipelining

objectives.text: Preserve per-connection output offsets across short sends, EINTR and EAGAIN without duplication or loss.
Queue bounded complete requests and emit corresponding responses in FIFO order under backpressure.
Stop later dispatch after close policy, then stage shutdown/drain/close without discarding the final response.

subtopics.title: Deadlines, resource limits and transport failure

objectives.text: Enforce independent idle, total-request, output and close-drain deadlines using injected monotonic time.
Handle readable hangup, half-close, incomplete body, broken output and reset as distinct outcomes.
Demonstrate bounded memory, connection count and descriptor ownership under slow or stalled peers.

subtopics.title: Parsing security and independent interoperability

objectives.text: Exercise framing-differential and optimistic-transition cases without claiming proxy/tunnel or TLS support.
Verify exact responses with independent curl/raw clients and compare semantic rather than packet-boundary results.
Publish a scope/evidence matrix showing original application C, OS-owned lower layers and remaining deployment limits.
